To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the self-force on a point charge in the presence of a quantum field is given by the sum of the classical Abraham-Lorentz force and a quantum stochastic force, which is the sum of the noise induced drift velocity and the noise induced velocity fluctuation.

the ALD-Langvin and MSTQW-Langvin equations are derived for the first time from quantum field theory in curved space, and that the stochastic drift motions are derived for the very first time in the literature.

we provide a quantum field-theoretic derivation of the Abraham- Lorentz-Dirac and the Mino- Sasaki- Tanaka-Quinn- Wald equations describing the motion of charged and uncharged particles, respectively, in curved space-time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantum and classical stochastic effects in electromagnetism and general relativity, and their applications to the study of gravitational waves.

the derivation of quantum mechanical self-force and stochastic equations for point charges and masses in curved spacetime, and their application to the study of stochastic particle motion in curved spacetime and the effect of stochastic forces on gravitational waves.
the derivation of the ALD and the MSTQWs equations from first principles in curved spacetime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-force is a classical effect of the quantum fields, and the stochastic force is a quantum effect of the quantum field.

the self-force and self-force-Langevin equations are derived from quantum fields in a curved space and are useful for studying the motion of charged and massive particles under the influence of self-force and stochastic noise sources.
the quantum field theory of a relativistic particle in curved space is now well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum field theoretic derivation of the ALD equation is the first of its kind and our derivation of the MSTQW and MSTQW-Langvin equations are novel and original.
the quantum fields in curved spacetime are capable of generating self-force on a particle, and the quantum fluctuations of the fields can cause stochastic motion of the particle.
we have developed a general framework for studying self-forces in quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quantum fluctuations in a field, which are usually ignored as being negligible, can have a significant effect on the motion of a particle sourcing the field.

the ALD equation and the MSTQQW equation are not the same, and the MSTQ equation does not have the runaway instability of the ALD equation, and hence is the correct equation for the self-force on a small mass in curved space.

the ALD and the MSTQQ equations, and their stochastic counterparts, are the most general self-force equations for point charges and point masses in curved spacetime, and they should be used for studying the dynamics of these objects.
